sources.title: Meta-Llama-3-8B model card
sources.evidence: Reopened October 27, 2026. The exact original base-model repository identifies Meta-Llama-3-8B; its Params table explicitly lists 8B, 8k context and GQA. The card distinguishes pretrained and instruction-tuned variants and gives Meta as developer, text input/output, April 18, 2024 release and the custom Llama 3 license. It links Llama 3.1 as a newer, separate model; no separate active-parameter value is specified.

sources.title: Original Meta Llama 3 model card
sources.evidence: Reopened October 27, 2026. The original release card explicitly distinguishes pretrained and instruction-tuned 8B and 70B models, describes autoregressive Transformers using GQA and 8,192-token training sequences, and reports the April 18, 2024 release. It supports the nominal 8B total but does not separately report activated parameters. Base benchmarks include prompted chain-of-thought tasks without specifying a dedicated reasoning mode.

sources.title: Introducing Meta Llama 3
sources.evidence: Reopened October 27, 2026. The April 18, 2024 announcement explicitly releases pretrained and instruction-fine-tuned language models with 8B and 70B parameters. It describes a standard decoder-only Transformer, GQA for both sizes, and training sequences of 8,192 tokens. It does not separately specify an active count.

sources.title: Original Llama 3 README
sources.evidence: Confirms release of model weights under license, an 8,192-token supported sequence limit, and separate pretrained versus instruction-tuned usage. Its exact Meta-Llama-3-8B example uses text completion; pretrained models are explicitly not fine-tuned for chat or Q&A.

sources.title: Original Llama 3 Transformer implementation
sources.evidence: TransformerBlock applies attention and a shared SwiGLU feed-forward network on every layer, with no expert router; GQA repeats key/value heads. This supports the dense architecture classification without using runtime cache defaults as the model context limit.

sources.title: Meta Llama 3 Community License Agreement
sources.evidence: Names the Meta Llama 3 Community License Agreement and April 18, 2024 version; grants limited rights over distributed weights and code subject to custom terms.

sources.title: Original Llama 3 generation implementation
sources.evidence: The documented base interface accepts plain string prompts and returns generated text with optional tokens and log probabilities. It provides no separately specified reasoning output or thinking-budget interface.

sources.title: Original Llama 3 tokenizer and chat format
sources.evidence: The original message structure has system, user and assistant roles with string content; special tokens do not define a separate reasoning channel. This does not itself prove that a model lacks general reasoning capability.

sources.title: Public metadata for the exact Meta-Llama-3-8B repository
sources.publisher: Hugging Face metadata for Meta repository
sources.evidence: Public metadata at revision 8cde5ca8380496c9a6cc7ef3a8b46a0372a1d920 reports safetensors.total=8030261248, entirely BF16, and LlamaForCausalLM. The aggregate does not expose tensor shapes or distinguish learned tensors from any persistent buffers; it is corroboration of the nominal scale, not an independently audited exact learned-parameter count.

sources.title: Exact Meta-Llama-3-8B checkpoint config
sources.evidence: The normal unauthenticated request returned HTTP 401. No access restriction was bypassed and no weight shards were downloaded.

sources.title: The Llama 3 Herd of Models, Table 1
sources.evidence: Table 1 explicitly gives original Llama 3 8B Finetuned=no, Tool use=no and Release=April 2024, separately from Llama 3.1. The paper states its later benchmark results describe Llama 3.1; those specifications are not transferred to this original checkpoint.

sources.title: Qwen3 Technical Report, Table 6: original Llama-3-8B Base
sources.evidence: Freshly opened October 27, 2026. Table 6 identifies Llama-3-8B with the explicit Base qualifier and lists Architecture=Dense, Total Params=8B and Activated Params=8B. The report separately identifies LLaMA-3.1-8B-Instruct elsewhere, so the Table 6 row is the original Llama 3 base model. This is the Qwen research team's explicit nominal comparison convention, not an active-count disclosure by Meta or an exact tensor census.

sources.title: DeepSeek-V2 technical report, Figure 1(a)
sources.evidence: Freshly opened October 27, 2026 and visually checked the original mmlu.svg plot. Figure 1(a) labels LLaMA 3 8B at approximately 8 billion on an axis explicitly named Activated Parameters (Billions). The May 2024 report compares pretrained models in Section 3.2 and discusses aligned chat models separately; this predates Llama 3.1. It corroborates the nominal scale under DeepSeek's comparison convention with approximate plot precision, not a direct Meta disclosure.

name.note: The original 8B pretrained model; the exact repository has no Instruct or 3.1 suffix.

developer.note: Meta is explicitly named as model developer.

family.note: Catalog key for the original Llama 3 family; the paper distinguishes it from Llama 3.1.

release_date.note: Day-precise original public release is stated by the card, announcement and license.

open_weights.note: Meta distributes pretrained weights under the custom license and access terms. Open weights does not imply unrestricted licensing.

license.note: Supported short name for the custom Meta Llama 3 Community License Agreement.

parameters_b.note: Meta explicitly publishes 8B for the original pretrained Llama 3 checkpoint. Retain this supported nominal total; an exact learned-tensor census is not required to establish the published size.

active_parameters_b.note: Qwen3 Table 6 explicitly reports 8B activated parameters for Llama-3-8B Base. DeepSeek-V2 Figure 1(a) independently places the original model at approximately 8B active. Adopt the Qwen authors' nominal comparison convention, not a direct Meta active-count disclosure or an inferred dense-equals-total rule; exact per-token tensor participation is not established.

architecture.note: The original decoder-only Transformer implementation uses attention plus dense SwiGLU feed-forward layers without expert routing; GQA is an attention design, not sparse expert activation.

context_window.note: The original README explicitly supports sequences up to 8,192 tokens. Later 128K Llama 3.1 specifications do not apply.

modalities.note: The card specifies text-only input and text/code output; code is represented as text.

reasoning.note: The original sources report general and prompted reasoning benchmarks but do not explicitly establish a dedicated reasoning mode. Plain completion code alone does not justify an affirmative or negative capability flag.

tool_call.note: Meta’s comparison Table 1 explicitly marks Tool use absent for the exact original Llama 3 8B base model. This concerns native support, not downstream wrappers or fine-tunes.

description.value: Meta’s original Llama 3 8B pretrained text-generation model, using a dense decoder-only Transformer with grouped-query attention and an 8,192-token context window.
description.note: Expands the accurate but sparse baseline description while identifying the base checkpoint and original architecture/context.

patch.description: Meta’s original Llama 3 8B pretrained text-generation model, using a dense decoder-only Transformer with grouped-query attention and an 8,192-token context window.
patch.notes: Total parameters are Meta’s nominal 8B. The nominal 8B active count follows the Qwen3 authors’ explicit comparison table for Llama-3-8B Base; it is not a separate Meta disclosure or an exact per-token tensor count. A dedicated reasoning mode remains unspecified. Meta marks native tool use absent for this original pretrained checkpoint.

Qwen3 Table 6: original Llama 3 8B Base activated parameters

summary: October 27 parameter re-audit retained Meta’s nominal 8B total after reopening the exact base card, original card and April release announcement. Fresh searches of Meta sources did not locate a separate active-count specification. Qwen3 Table 6 explicitly identifies the original Llama-3-8B Base and reports 8B activated parameters; this supports changing active_parameters_b from undisclosed to verified at nominal 8B under the Qwen authors’ stated comparison convention. DeepSeek-V2 Figure 1(a), visually inspected, corroborates approximately 8B active. Neither comparison is represented as a direct Meta active-count disclosure or exact per-token tensor census. All twelve nonparameter assessments are preserved.
